data.description: Superflat‌[JE  only] or Flat world‌[BE  only] is a world type or a vanilla world preset that replaces the normal varied terrain of the Overworld with a completely flat surface composed of multiple layers and set to a single biome.

<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Default_Superflat_world.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Default_Superflat_world.png/300px-Default_Superflat_world.png?a0fc8" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Default_Superflat_world.png/600px-Default_Superflat_world.png?a0fc8 2x" data-file-width="854" data-file-height="480"></a><figcaption>A default superflat world</figcaption></figure>
<p><b>Superflat</b>‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> or <b>Flat world</b>‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">BE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> is a <a href="/w/World_type" title="World type">world type</a> or a vanilla <a href="/w/World_preset" title="World preset">world preset</a> that replaces the normal varied terrain of the <a href="/w/Overworld" title="Overworld">Overworld</a> with a completely flat surface composed of multiple layers and set to a single <a href="/w/Biome" title="Biome">biome</a>.
</p><p>A superflat world can be customized using presets, which change its layers and biome. In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, presets can also change the <a href="/w/Feature" title="Feature">features</a> and <a href="/w/Structure" title="Structure">structures</a> found in a superflat world, and an in-game menu allows players to fully customize the layers and the biome.
</p><p>In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, superflat can also refer to a dimension's generator type, with which the completely flat terrain can be generated in a specific dimension. See also <a href="/w/Custom_dimension" class="mw-redirect" title="Custom dimension">Custom dimension</a> and <a href="/w/Custom_world_preset" class="mw-redirect" title="Custom world preset">Custom world preset</a>.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Structure">Structure</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=1&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Structure" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section's source code: Structure"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In the default superflat world, the terrain consists of one layer of <a href="/w/Bedrock" title="Bedrock">bedrock</a>, two layers of <a href="/w/Dirt" title="Dirt">dirt</a>, and one layer of <a href="/w/Grass_block" class="mw-redirect" title="Grass block">grass blocks</a>, with the <a href="/w/Biome" title="Biome">biome</a> set to <a href="/w/Plains" title="Plains">plains</a>. In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, <a href="/w/Village" title="Village">villages</a> generate relatively frequently, and <a href="/w/Stronghold" title="Stronghold">strongholds</a> can also be found; in <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, no features or structures generate in flat worlds.
</p><p>In the default superflat world, the surface of the world is completely flat and at Y=-60, except for villages and other structures if they are enabled. <a href="/w/Mob" title="Mob">Mobs</a> still spawn normally. Because of the low <a href="/w/Altitude" title="Altitude">altitude</a> of the world, <a href="/w/Slime" title="Slime">slimes</a> spawn frequently.
</p><p>Superflat worlds allow the player to access <a href="/w/The_Nether" title="The Nether">the Nether</a> and <a href="/w/The_End" title="The End">the End</a> in the usual ways, which generate as normal.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Customization">Customization</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=2&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Customization" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section's source code: Customization"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>When <a href="/w/Create_New_World" title="Create New World">creating a new world</a>, the superflat generator can be changed to various presets or fully customized depending on the edition.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Java_Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=3&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Java Edition" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=3" title="Edit section's source code: Java Edition"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Superflat_Button.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Superflat_Button.png/300px-Superflat_Button.png?8cb95" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="19" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Superflat_Button.png/600px-Superflat_Button.png?8cb95 2x" data-file-width="930" data-file-height="60"></a><figcaption>The Superflat world type button in <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Superflat_Customisation.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Superflat_Customisation.png/300px-Superflat_Customisation.png?62ea9" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Superflat_Customisation.png/600px-Superflat_Customisation.png?62ea9 2x" data-file-width="854" data-file-height="480"></a><figcaption>The Superflat Customization screen, which appears after the "Customize" button is clicked</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:Superflat_Presets.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/Superflat_Presets.png/300px-Superflat_Presets.png?1c2e4" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/thumb/Superflat_Presets.png/600px-Superflat_Presets.png?1c2e4 2x" data-file-width="854" data-file-height="480"></a><figcaption>The Select a Preset screen, which shows some predefined presets and also allows the player to customize the preset</figcaption></figure>
<p>In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, upon selecting "Superflat" in the "World Type" button, the "Customize" button on its right becomes clickable. In the "Superflat Customization" menu, there are two buttons available to customize superflat worlds: the "Remove Layer" button, used for removing unwanted types of layers, and the "Presets" button, used for accessing the <i>preset code string</i> or selecting one of the nine <i>default presets</i>. <a href="/w/Data_pack" title="Data pack">Data packs</a> can be used to customize the default presets or add new ones, see <a href="/w/Custom_world_preset#Superflat_Level_Generation_Preset" class="mw-redirect" title="Custom world preset">Custom world preset#Superflat Level Generation Preset</a> for more information.
</p><p>If the player can understand the <a href="#Preset_code_format">preset code syntax</a>, they can create presets of their own by entering valid information into the preset code box. The preset code can be highlighted and copied, allowing it to be shared with other players. Similar to how new worlds are shared through <a href="/w/Seed_(world_generation)" class="mw-redirect" title="Seed (world generation)">seeds</a>, a preset code can be entered into this box to use it.
</p><p>The preset code currently cannot fully describe a superflat level generation preset. Settings related to features and structures are inaccessible in the preset code. Using a preset code to recreate a world can only ensure that the blocks on each layer are the same, as well as the same biome, but cannot guarantee the same settings for features or structures. When using a preset code, the settings for features and structures are based on what default preset is currently selected on the list.
</p>
<ul><li>If no preset is selected, only <a href="/w/Village" title="Village">villages</a> and <a href="/w/Stronghold" title="Stronghold">strongholds</a> are generated.</li>
<li>If the "Classic Flat" preset is selected, only villages are generated.</li>
<li>If the "Overworld" preset is selected, all <a href="/w/Feature" title="Feature">features</a> in the <a href="/w/Plains" title="Plains">plains biome</a> (except <a href="/w/Monster_room" class="mw-redirect" title="Monster room">monster rooms</a>), <a href="/w/Pillager_outpost" class="mw-redirect" title="Pillager outpost">pillager outposts</a>, villages, strongholds, <a href="/w/Mineshaft" title="Mineshaft">mineshafts</a>, and <a href="/w/Ruined_portal" class="mw-redirect" title="Ruined portal">ruined portals</a> are generated.</li>
<li>Note that for structures to be generated (on any preset), there is a separate setting "Generate structures" available in the <a href="/w/Create_New_World#World" title="Create New World">world creation screen</a> which must be set to ON (the default setting).</li></ul>
<div class="" style="clear:both"></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Bedrock_Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=4&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Bedrock Edition" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section's source code: Bedrock Edition"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, upon enabling "Flat world" in the "Advanced" settings tab, an additional setting allows the player to select a preset and view its block layers. Presets only affect the layers and the biome; terrain features and structures never generate in any of the presets.
</p><p>There is no interface for further customization. However, custom flat worlds are possible internally, and can be generated by modifying <code>FlatWorldLayers</code> in the world's <code>level.dat</code> file using an external editor. This was used for converting custom superflat worlds from <a href="/w/Legacy_Console_Edition" title="Legacy Console Edition">Legacy Console Edition</a> to the console versions of <i>Bedrock Edition</i>.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Legacy_Console_Edition"><i>Legacy Console Edition</i></h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=5&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Legacy Console Edition" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section's source code: Legacy Console Edition"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/w/File:LCE_Superflat_Customization_Button.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="/images/thumb/LCE_Superflat_Customization_Button.png/300px-LCE_Superflat_Customization_Button.png?c64a9" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="300" height="51" class="mw-file-element" srcset="/images/LCE_Superflat_Customization_Button.png?c64a9 2x" data-file-width="461" data-file-height="79"></a><figcaption>The "Customize Superflat" button in <a href="/w/Legacy_Console_Edition" title="Legacy Console Edition">Legacy Console Edition</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>In <a href="/w/Legacy_Console_Edition" title="Legacy Console Edition">Legacy Console Edition</a>, upon enabling "Superflat World" under the "More Options" menu, the "Customize Superflat" button becomes clickable, allowing the player to customize each block layer, the biome of the world, and the properties of generated terrain features and structures, as well as select one of the default presets.
</p><p>By default, the world is set to the Plains biome, and <a href="/w/Village" title="Village">villages</a> are the only generated feature in the Overworld.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Preset_code_format">Preset code format</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=7&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Preset code format" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section's source code: Preset code format"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div class="msgbox searchaux msgbox-mini msgbox-blue" style="max-width: 50em;">
<div class="msgbox-icon"> <div class="msgbox-image" style=""> <span class="mw-valign-text-top" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/w/File:Information_icon.svg" title="File:Information icon.svg"><img alt="" src="/images/Information_icon.svg?15c1c" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="62" data-file-height="62"></a></span></div>
</div>
<div style="width: 100%;"><div style="font-weight: bold; display: inline">This feature is exclusive to <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>.</div> 
</div>
</div>
<p>The preset code is a string of numbers, semicolons(;), colons(:), commas(,), and asterisks(*). Each code has three main parts, divided by semicolons. They are:
</p>
<ul><li>a list of one or more <a href="/w/Java_Edition_data_values" title="Java Edition data values"><b>block IDs</b></a>;
<ul><li>The block list is a comma-separated list of block IDs, ordered from <a href="/w/Altitude" title="Altitude">layer -64 up</a>; if the entry for a given block has an "*", the number before the "*" is the number of layers to be generated, and the string after is the block ID.</li>
<li>A block can also be repeated over multiple layers simply by repeating the block's ID, e.g. <code>minecraft:glass,minecraft:glass,minecraft:glass,minecraft:glass</code> would give the same result as <code>4*minecraft:glass</code>.</li></ul></li>
<li>a valid <a href="/w/Java_Edition_data_values" title="Java Edition data values"><b>biome ID</b></a>;</li>
<li>(optional, <b>not after 1.16</b>) a list of <b>feature generation options</b>.
<ul><li>Feature generation options (described below) may have additional parameters, for example <code>village(size=0 distance=9)</code> (in 1.13+ they have no effect). Multiple parameters are separated by spaces, rather than commas or semicolons.</li></ul></li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Feature_generation_options">Feature generation options</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=8&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Feature generation options" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section's source code: Feature generation options"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

<p>Several criteria must be satisfied before some features can appear:
</p>
<ul><li>The biome ID must be correct. For example, at present villages can appear only in biome IDs <code>plains</code>, <code>desert</code>, <code>taiga</code>, <code>savanna</code>, <code>snowy_taiga</code>, and <code>snowy_tundra</code>.</li>
<li>Structures must be turned on when creating new world. (This does not affect normal features such as trees, flowers, mushrooms, and giant mushrooms.)</li>
<li>There must be suitable terrain for the structure to appear on or in. This applies to most features except for mineshafts and strongholds.
<ul><li>Villages are a partial exception; they do not form in mid-air, but can form provided there is at least one solid block layer.
<ul><li>Villages always spawn at least 2 blocks above the void.</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>
<p>For example, to have an 'End' superflat world with <a href="/w/End_spike" class="mw-redirect" title="End spike">end spikes</a>, the biome ID must be <code>the_end</code>, and the top surface block must be <a href="/w/End_stone" class="mw-redirect" title="End stone">end stone</a>. In this particular case 'Structures' does not need to be turned on in the world options.
</p><p>Attempting to use an incorrectly formatted preset code causes the game to default to the Classic preset.
</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Preset_code_example">Preset code example</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=9&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Preset code example" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section's source code: Preset code example"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Consider the following preset code: 
</p>
<pre style="word-break:break-all">minecraft:mossy_cobblestone,250*minecraft:air,minecraft:obsidian,minecraft:snow;minecraft:plains</pre>
<p>It consists of the following elements:
</p>
<ul><li><code>minecraft:mossy_cobblestone,250*minecraft:air,minecraft:obsidian,minecraft:snow</code> — comma-separated list of <a href="/w/Java_Edition_data_values#Block_IDs" title="Java Edition data values">block IDs</a>.
<ul><li><code>minecraft:mossy_cobblestone</code> — one layer of <a href="/w/Mossy_cobblestone" class="mw-redirect" title="Mossy cobblestone">mossy cobblestone</a> on layer -64.</li>
<li><code>250*minecraft:air</code> — 250 layers of <a href="/w/Air" title="Air">air</a>, from layer -63 to layer 186.</li>
<li><code>minecraft:obsidian</code> — one layer of <a href="/w/Obsidian" title="Obsidian">obsidian</a>, on layer 187.</li>
<li><code>minecraft:snow</code> — one layer of <a href="/w/Snow" title="Snow">snow</a>, on layer 188.</li></ul></li>
<li><code>minecraft:plains</code> — <a href="/w/Java_Edition_data_values#Biome_IDs" title="Java Edition data values">biome ID</a>, in this case Plains.</li></ul>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Multiplayer">Multiplayer</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=10&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Multiplayer" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section's source code: Multiplayer"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, the <code>level-type</code> flag in <samp><a href="/w/Server.properties" title="Server.properties">server.properties</a></samp> must be set to <code>minecraft\:flat</code> for a <a href="/w/Server" title="Server">server</a> to generate as superflat.
</p><p>The JSON object flag <code>generator-settings</code> in <samp><a href="/w/Server.properties" title="Server.properties">server.properties</a></samp> defines further customizations of the world, such as block layers, biome, and structures. The syntax is shown in the example below:
</p>
<div class="treeview">
<ul><li><span title="NBT Compound / JSON Object"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-48px -16px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[NBT Compound / JSON Object]</span></span>: The root object.
<ul><li class="mw-empty-elt"></li><li class="treeview-header nbttree-inherited load-page" data-page="Template:Nbt inherit/flat generator settings/template" data-template="true" data-treeview="true" data-treeviewclass="nbttree-inherited">Flat generation settings<span class="noscript"> see <a href="/w/Template:Nbt_inherit/flat_generator_settings/template" title="Template:Nbt inherit/flat generator settings/template">Template:Nbt inherit/flat generator settings/template</a></span></li></ul></li></ul>
</div><p>Example generation settings that recreate the "Classic Flat" preset:</p><div class="mw-highlight mw-highlight-lang-properties mw-content-ltr" dir="ltr"><pre><span></span><span class="na">generator-settings</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s">{"biome":"minecraft:plains","layers":[{"block":"minecraft:bedrock","height":1},{"block":"minecraft:dirt","height":2},{"block":"minecraft:grass_block","height":1}]}</span>
<span class="na">level-type</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s">minecraft</span><span class="se">\:</span><span class="s">flat</span>
</pre></div><p>In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, setting the <i>level-type</i> field in <a href="/w/Server.properties" title="Server.properties">server.properties</a> to "FLAT" will generate a flat world.
</p><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="History">History</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=11&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: History" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section's source code: History"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

Issues should be reported and viewed <a target="_blank" rel="nofollow noreferrer noopener" class="external text" href="https://bugs.mojang.com/issues/?jql=project%20in%20%28MC%2C%20MCPE%29%20AND%20%28resolution%20is%20EMPTY%20OR%20resolution%20in%20%281%2C%202%2C%206%29%29%20AND%20%28summary%20~%20%22Superflat%22%20OR%20summary%20~%20%22Flat%20worlds%22%29%20ORDER%20BY%20resolution%20DESC">there</a>.

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Trivia">Trivia</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Superflat?section=17&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Trivia" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Superflat?action=edit&section=17" title="Edit section's source code: Trivia"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<ul><li>Superflat was first conceived at the first <a href="/w/MINECON" title="MINECON">MINECON</a> and was intended for <a href="/w/Creative" title="Creative">Creative</a> builds, but is a good Survival challenge.<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></li>
<li>If a superflat world is upgraded from 1.17 or before to 1.18.2 or later, any structure that generates in a plains biome now generates.</li></ul>
